[USER] User inquired about the popularity of reggae music as a cultural movement in Jamaica and worldwide.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Reggae music originated in Jamaica in the late 1960s and was influenced by African rhythms, ska, and rocksteady music.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Reggae gained popularity among the working-class population in Jamaica with catchy beats and socially conscious lyrics focusing on poverty, oppression, and resistance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Reggae music became associated with the Rastafarian movement, promoting a spiritual connection between Jamaica and Africa and encouraging social and political change.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Prominent reggae musicians, such as Bob Marley, were followers of the Rastafarian movement and used their music to spread their message.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1970s, reggae music spread beyond Jamaica, gaining popularity in Europe and the United States due to Jamaican sound systems and the growth of the Jamaican music industry.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bob Marley became an international superstar, helping to popularize reggae music worldwide.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Reggae music continues to be a popular cultural movement in Jamaica and globally, with diverse artists and styles reflecting the genre's roots and evolution.

6. Bunny Wailer - a founding member of The Wailers and an important reggae artist.  
7. Dennis Brown - a smooth-voiced reggae singer who recorded over 75 albums.
